# Deep Funding Originality: Round 3

How much of an open-source repository's value is its own work, and how much comes from the dependencies it builds on? Predict an **originality score between 0 and 1** for each of the **98 repositories** in Deep Funding Round 3.

Human jurors rate each repository's originality on a 0–100 scale. A repository's answer is the average of its jurors' ratings, divided by 100. The same averages resolve the Round 3 originality markets on [deep.seer.pm](https://deep.seer.pm).

## What to predict

The share of each repository's value that is original work rather than carried by its dependencies:

| Originality | Typical repository |
|---|---|
| 0.2 | A fork or thin wrapper: far less work went into the project than into what it builds on (Brave on Chromium, Ollama on llama.cpp). |
| 0.5 | Leans heavily on its dependencies, but has also done a large amount of work in its own right (an Ethereum wallet). |
| 0.8 | Mostly original: its dependencies are fairly generic, and it could have been built without them if needed. |

## Scoring

Your **error** is the sum, over the scored repositories, of the absolute difference between your originality and the jurors' average originality. **Lower is better.** This is the scoring rule of the earlier Deep Funding originality contest on Pond.

## Leaderboards

- **Public leaderboard:** the 33 repositories rated in Deep Funding's first originality jury round (Originality R1). Those ratings are public and included in the [competition dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DeepFunding/originality-r3-data), so the public leaderboard is a check of your file and method, not a preview of the final standings.
- **Private leaderboard (final):** the Round 3 jurors' averages for the repositories evaluated in Round 3. These ratings do not exist yet. They are added when the Round 3 originality markets resolve, every submission is then re-scored, and the private leaderboard decides the final standings. Until then a submission's private score is a placeholder equal to its public score.

**Only your latest submission counts.** When submissions close, each team's most recent scored submission becomes its final entry. Earlier submissions don't count, even if they scored better, and there is no picking the best of two. The submission selection option on the My submissions page has no effect.

## Prize distribution

| Place | Prize |
|---|---|
| 1st | $1,000 |
| 2nd | $650 |
| 3rd | $350 |

Prizes go to the top three eligible teams on the final private leaderboard, scored once the Round 3 originality markets on deep.seer.pm resolve. Submissions close December 10, 2026, 23:59 UTC.

## Trading on deep.seer.pm

The submission file has the same format deep.seer.pm takes, so the CSV you submit here can also be uploaded at [deep.seer.pm](https://deep.seer.pm) to trade the Round 3 originality markets.

**A minimum trade of $10 in sUSDS on the Round 3 originality markets is required to be eligible for prizes.** Even if a submission places in the top 3, it does not count unless its team has made that $10 trade on Seer, and the next eligible team moves up. The organizers manually verify the trades of the top 3 submissions only.

- **Questions, or $10 in trading credits for prize eligibility:** the public [Telegram group](https://t.me/agentallocators).
